summary: Imre Hamar is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University around 1997 and a visiting professor at Otani University.

In-gun Kang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Kang studied at the Jesuit School of Theology of Santa Clara University, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under several teachers, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes for a doctorate.

Ines Konczak is a specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Konczak has served as a postdoctoral research fellow at Staatliche Museen zu Berlin and was a visiting research fellow at Ryukoku University in 2012.

Ingmar Heise is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. Heise earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and pursued doctoral studies as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol.

Ingo Strauch is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He became a professor at the University of Lausanne around 2014 and has taught Andrea Schlosser and Kathrin Holz.

Inyoung Chung is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia in 2008 under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner, with Karen C. Lang, Cynthia Hoehler-Fatton, Ronald G. Dimberg, and Hyangsoon Yi serving on the committee.

Irach J. S. Taraporewala (1884–1956) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Comparative Philology at the University of Calcutta (~1917–1930) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (1954–1955).

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy specializes in Tibetology. She studied at Free University of Brussels (~1990–2004), Tibet University, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Harvard University. In 2007, she held a post teaching Anthropology at Laval University.
Isabelle Onians is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a PhD at the University of Oxford (~1997–2002) and served as an editor for the Clay Sanskrit Library (~2005–2009).

Isabelle Ratié is an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Paris 1, EPHE, and under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig University, University of Paris, Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2014–2025), and Collège de France (2025).
Isaline Blew Horner (1896–1981) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Newnham College (~1914–1917) and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society (~1942–1969).

Iselin Frydenlund is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. Frydenlund was a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo (~2007–2012) and a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo (~2012–2015).

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar (1820–1891) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School and Sanskrit College and University until around 1841, later serving as Direttore of Sanskrit College and University (~1851–1858).
Issaen Ikeyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts as a professor (教授) at Shitennoji Junior College and at Eizan Gakuin.
Issei Suzuki (b. 1863) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and later held a post there as professor (教授).
Issei Yamakawa (b. 1937) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Yamakawa studied at Sophia University and completed a master's program (修士課程) at Aichi Gakuin University.

Ivan Minayev (1840–1890) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University (~1869–1890), where his students included Sergey Oldenburg and Fyodor Shcherbatskoy.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev (1840–1890) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. In 1863, he studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Albrecht Weber. He later taught Theodore Stcherbatsky.
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa (1970–1988), and taught David P. Jackson.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned a PhD at Harvard (~1996–2003) under Leonard van der Kuijp, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College (~2002–2003).
